expectations.text: States that a written agreement or reminder is not enforcement
expectations.evidence: "You've now delivered the same rule through three channels... are all the same device — training... the 50% number is the measurement of how well training works. Rung 0 (docs, reminders, review checklists) → you need rung 1 (impossible) or rung 2."

expectations.text: Recommends a pre-commit hook to run the formatter automatically
expectations.evidence: "Pre-commit hook that auto-fixes and re-stages, not one that scolds." Provides ruff-format config.

expectations.text: Notes that pre-commit is bypassable with --no-verify and must be backed by a CI check
expectations.evidence: "Three layers, cheapest first:... Pre-commit hook... CI check as the authority, because --no-verify exists."

expectations.text: Recommends a type check as a required CI check
expectations.evidence: "Type annotations can't be auto-fixed, so it's a ratchet problem." Provides CI job for types check.

expectations.text: Recommends baselining or ratcheting rather than enforcing across the whole repo at once
expectations.evidence: "Enforce on changed files only. The violation count can then only go down."

expectations.text: Notes that branch protection is what makes a CI check actually required
expectations.evidence: "Branch protection with these as required checks. Without it, both jobs are advisory and you've built a more elaborate reminder." Provides gh api command.

expectations.text: Recommends the failure message tell the developer how to fix it
expectations.evidence: "Make the failure teach. error: rule violated produces a workaround... Unformatted files. Run: ruff format . — or enable format-on-save so this never fires again produces a fix."

expectations.text: Does not primarily recommend rewriting CONTRIBUTING.md, more reminders, or more discipline
expectations.evidence: Primary recommendations are devices. CONTRIBUTING.md edit is secondary: "Finally: replace the CONTRIBUTING.md paragraph with one line pointing at the checks."
